definitions.explanation: A popular Chinese-origin dish of soft tofu in a spicy sauce made with minced meat, chili bean paste, and Sichuan peppercorns. Widely eaten in Japan.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}の{昼|ひる}ご{飯|はん}は{麻婆豆腐|まーぼーどうふ}にした。
examples.english: I had mapo tofu for lunch today.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}の{麻婆豆腐|まーぼーどうふ}は{辛|から}くて{美味|おい}しい。
examples.english: This restaurant's mapo tofu is spicy and delicious.

examples.japanese: {麻婆豆腐|まーぼーどうふ}の{素|もと}を{使|つか}えば、{家|いえ}でも{簡単|かんたん}に{本格的|ほんかくてき}な{味|あじ}が{楽|たの}しめる。
examples.english: If you use a mapo tofu sauce mix, you can easily enjoy an authentic flavor at home.

notes:
Originally a Sichuan dish from China, {麻婆豆腐|まーぼーどうふ} became one of the most popular Chinese dishes in Japan. The name comes from Chinese: {麻|まー} (numbing, from Sichuan pepper) + {婆|ぼー} (old woman, referring to the dish's legendary creator) + {豆腐|どうふ} (tofu).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {麻婆豆腐|まーぼーどうふ}を{作|つく}る: to make mapo tofu
- {麻婆豆腐|まーぼーどうふ}の{素|もと}: mapo tofu sauce mix
- {麻婆豆腐|まーぼーどうふ}{丼|どん}: mapo tofu rice bowl
- {辛口|からくち}{麻婆豆腐|まーぼーどうふ}: spicy mapo tofu
- {本格|ほんかく}{麻婆豆腐|まーぼーどうふ}: authentic mapo tofu

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, {麻婆豆腐|まーぼーどうふ} is a staple of {中華料理|ちゅうかりょうり} (Chinese cuisine) and a common home-cooked meal. Instant sauce packets ({麻婆豆腐|まーぼーどうふ}の{素|もと}) are sold in every supermarket. The Japanese version tends to be milder than the Sichuan original.

RELATED DISHES:
- {麻婆|まーぼー}なす: mapo eggplant — same sauce with eggplant instead of tofu
- {回鍋肉|ほいこーろー}: twice-cooked pork — another popular Chinese dish in Japan
- {青椒肉絲|ちんじゃおろーすー}: pepper steak — stir-fried beef with green peppers
